blockMcqs.question: What are the two core jobs of a router?
options: Encryption and compression
Forwarding packets and building routing tables
Assigning IP addresses and caching DNS
Filtering spam and logging traffic
blockMcqs.explanation: Forwarding moves individual packets; routing builds and maintains the table used for forwarding.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement best describes forwarding?
options: Exchanging routing tables with neighbors every 30 seconds
Deciding which interface to send each incoming packet out on
Building a shortest-path tree of the whole network
Assigning IP subnets to new routers
blockMcqs.explanation: Forwarding is the per-packet data-plane action: look up the destination and send it out the right interface.

blockMcqs.question: A routing table has two matching rows for a destination. How does the router choose?
options: It picks the row added most recently
It picks the row with the lowest metric
It picks the row with the longest matching prefix
It picks the first row listed
blockMcqs.explanation: Longest-prefix match selects the most specific route, giving fine-grained control over traffic paths.

blockMcqs.question: What does a host do with traffic destined outside its local subnet?
options: Broadcasts it to all devices on the LAN
Drops the packet and logs an error
Sends it to the DNS resolver
Forwards it to its configured default gateway
blockMcqs.explanation: The default gateway is the exit router for all off-subnet traffic; the host has no direct route elsewhere.

blockMcqs.question: Which is an advantage of dynamic routing over static routing?
options: Zero CPU overhead
Simpler configuration for large networks
Automatic recovery when a link fails
Guaranteed shortest path every time
blockMcqs.explanation: Dynamic protocols detect topology changes and recompute paths; static routes stay fixed even after a failure.

blockMcqs.question: What does a distance-vector router share with its neighbors?
options: Its full network topology map
Only the IP of the default gateway
Its own routing table (distances to all destinations)
A list of all MAC addresses it knows
blockMcqs.explanation: Distance-vector routers advertise their routing tables; neighbors update their own based on what they hear.

blockMcqs.question: Which algorithm does OSPF use to find the best paths?
options: Bellman-Ford
Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm
Binary search
Round-robin selection
blockMcqs.explanation: Link-state routers have the full topology, so each runs Dijkstra independently to compute shortest paths.

blockMcqs.question: Which protocol connects different organizations on the public internet?
options: RIP
OSPF
BGP
ICMP
blockMcqs.explanation: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) connects autonomous systems and is the routing protocol that holds the internet together.
